title: Mendez v. Crestline Logistics: Warehouse Forkift Collision
premise: A forklift collided with a worker in a warehouse during a night shift.

side_A.role: a lawyer representing the injured worker
side_A.goal: building a negligence claim against the employer

side_B.role: a claims investigator for the employer's insurer
side_B.goal: assessing whether the worker's own conduct caused the injury

=== DOCUMENT 1: Crestline Logistics Incident Log ===

**CRESTLINE LOGISTICS — INCIDENT REPORT LOG**
**Facility:** Building 7, Trenton Industrial Park
**Report No.:** CL-2024-0314-007
**Date of Incident:** March 14, 2024
**Time of Incident:** 11:47 PM
**Reported By:** Raymond Tufo, Shift Supervisor
**Date Filed:** March 15, 2024, 12:34 AM

**INCIDENT TYPE:** Vehicle-pedestrian collision (forklift)

**LOCATION:** Aisle 14, Building 7, Crestline Logistics Distribution Center. Aisle 14 is designated as a shared traffic lane for both forklifts and foot workers.

**INDIVIDUALS INVOLVED:**
- Juan Mendez, Floor Associate — injured party. Employee tenure: 3 years, 2 months as of March 14, 2024.
- David Kowalski, Forklift Operator — vehicle operator. Forklift operating experience at Crestline Logistics: 6 years. Current OSHA forklift certification, valid through September 2024.

**EQUIPMENT INVOLVED:** 2019 Toyota 8FGCU25 propane forklift, maximum load capacity 5,000 pounds. Unit No. FL-07.

**SHIFT STAFFING:** Night shift, March 14, 2024. Total assigned personnel: 18 workers. Typical daytime complement: 24. Building 7 was staffed at 75% of daytime levels.

**DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT:**
At approximately 11:47 PM on March 14, 2024, a forklift operated by David Kowalski collided with warehouse worker Juan Mendez in Aisle 14 of Building 7. The forklift's event data recorder was downloaded the following morning and logged a travel speed of 6.2 miles per hour at the moment of impact. The data recorder also confirmed that the forklift's strobe light was activated at the time of the collision.

Per Crestline's energy conservation night-shift policy, the warehouse was illuminated at 60% of standard capacity on the evening of the incident.

**POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS:**
- Emergency medical services were contacted at 11:49 PM.
- Juan Mendez was transported by ambulance to Mercer County General Hospital, where he was admitted for surgery. He remained hospitalized for 4 days.
- The backup alarm on the forklift was tested after the incident and found to be fully functional.
- Post-incident toxicology screening of David Kowalski was conducted at 1:15 AM on March 15, 2024, at Mercer County General Hospital. Results returned negative for alcohol and controlled substances.

**SAFETY EQUIPMENT:** Crestline Logistics requires all warehouse floor workers to wear high-visibility reflective vests during night shifts. Vests were issued to all employees on site that evening.

**SAFETY MANUAL REFERENCE:** Crestline Logistics safety manual specifies a maximum forklift speed of 5 miles per hour in all warehouse aisles.

**PRIOR INCIDENTS:** Crestline Logistics records show 3 documented forklift-related near-miss incidents in Building 7 during the 6 months prior to March 14, 2024.

**REGULATORY NOTIFICATION:** The incident was reported to OSHA on March 15, 2024. An OSHA inspection was conducted on March 19, 2024.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Medical Report and Billing Summary ===

**MERCER COUNTY GENERAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT REPORT**
**Patient:** Juan Mendez
**DOB:** [On file]
**Date of Admission:** March 15, 2024, 12:14 AM
**Date of Discharge:** March 19, 2024
**Attending Physician:** Dr. Sarah Whitfield, Orthopedic Surgery

**PRESENTATION:**
Patient arrived via ambulance following a forklift-pedestrian collision at a warehouse facility. Patient was alert and oriented on arrival. Primary survey revealed significant trauma to the right lower extremity, left thorax, and left forearm.

**INJURIES DOCUMENTED:**
1. Fractured right tibia — closed fracture, mid-shaft, requiring open reduction and internal fixation.
2. Two cracked ribs — left side, ribs 6 and 7. No pneumothorax observed.
3. Laceration to left forearm — measured approximately 9 cm in length, extending through dermis. Repaired in the emergency department with 14 stitches prior to surgery.

**TREATMENT:**
- Emergency department stabilization and wound closure (left forearm laceration, 14 stitches).
- Surgical intervention on March 15, 2024, for open reduction and internal fixation of the right tibial fracture. Procedure performed by Dr. Sarah Whitfield. No intraoperative complications.
- Pain management and monitoring during inpatient stay.

**HOSPITAL COURSE:**
Patient was admitted to the orthopedic inpatient unit following surgery. Recovery was unremarkable. Patient was discharged on March 19, 2024, after 4 days of hospitalization with instructions for non-weight-bearing on the right lower extremity and follow-up with orthopedics in 2 weeks.

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Patient was seen for follow-up appointments on April 2, April 16, April 30, May 14, May 28, and June 11, 2024. Progress notes indicate gradual healing of the tibial fracture. Patient remained off work for 11 weeks following the incident and had not returned to work as of June 30, 2024.
